source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-274911:If the raid begins more than 112 blocks above the ground, all illagers will be summoned and the player wins
source_meta._title: Raid results in victory if it cannot find a valid spawn point

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4, vanilla client, single-player integrated server, a newly created Superflat Overworld, Creative mode, cheats enabled, Normal difficulty, and raids enabled. The reproduction uses a minimal claimed-bed village on an enclosed glass platform around Y=200 so that the platform itself does not provide valid raid-spawn surfaces and the Superflat ground is far below it.
preconditions: Launch the exact affected version 1.14.4 rather than the fix version 24w33a or any later release.
Use an unmodified vanilla installation with no mods, datapacks, or previously created village points of interest affecting the test area.
The executor must be able to run commands from in-game chat; all commands below include the leading slash and require cheats.

Use the default control bindings unless controls have been rebound: T opens chat, E opens the inventory, number keys select hotbar slots, right-click uses or places an item, and double-tapping Space toggles Creative flight.
Keep the villager and its claimed bed intact through the trigger step.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select and start the Java Edition installation for version 1.14.4. Do not select 24w33a or another fix/later version.
steps.success_cue: The main-menu version label identifies the running game as Minecraft Java Edition 1.14.4.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, cycle World Type to Superflat, and create the world. Leave the Superflat preset at its default so that the ordinary ground remains far below the planned sky village.
steps.success_cue: A new Superflat world opens and the player can fly and use commands.

steps.action: Wait before issuing commands until the nearby Superflat terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The nearby flat terrain is visible, movement is responsive, and no world-loading screen is present.

steps.action: Press T, enter the difficulty command exactly as supplied, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the difficulty was set to Normal.

steps.action: Press T, enter the gamerule command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to ensure that raid triggering is not disabled.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that disableRaids is set to false.

steps.action: Press T, enter the teleport command exactly as supplied, and press Enter. Wait for the player to settle onto the Superflat terrain near the origin; the purpose is to make all later structure coordinates deterministic.
steps.success_cue: The player is near X=0 and Z=0 on the Superflat ground, with movement responsive after teleportation.

steps.action: Press T, enter the fill command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to create the 9-by-9 glass floor of the sky village at Y=199.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that blocks were filled at the requested coordinates.

steps.action: Press T, enter the fill command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to create the north glass wall.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the north wall blocks were filled.

steps.action: Press T, enter the fill command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to create the south glass wall.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the south wall blocks were filled.

steps.action: Press T, enter the fill command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to create the west glass wall between the previously created north and south walls.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the west wall blocks were filled.

steps.action: Press T, enter the fill command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to create the east glass wall between the previously created north and south walls.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the east wall blocks were filled; the resulting structure has a glass floor, three-block-high glass perimeter walls, and an open roof.

steps.action: Press T, enter the teleport command exactly as supplied, and press Enter. Wait for the sky platform to render completely.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing inside the glass enclosure around Y=200, the entire floor and perimeter walls are visible, and the low Superflat ground is far below.

steps.action: Press T, enter the give command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to obtain one white bed.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that a white bed was given, and a white-bed item is visible in the inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Select the white bed in the active hotbar slot. If it is not already in the hotbar, press E, move it into any hotbar slot, close the inventory, and press that slot's number key. Look at a glass floor block near the center of the enclosure with at least one adjacent unobstructed floor block, then right-click once to place the bed. Do not place it against a wall.
steps.success_cue: A complete two-block white bed is present near the center of the glass enclosure, with open space allowing a villager to reach it.

steps.action: Press T, enter the summon command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to create a villager inside the enclosure.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that a villager was summoned, and one villager is visible inside the glass enclosure without falling from the platform.

steps.action: Press T, enter the time command exactly as supplied, and press Enter. Move away from the bed so that the villager has an unobstructed path to it.
steps.success_cue: The world becomes nighttime and the villager can walk to the bed.

steps.action: Wait until the villager reaches the bed and lies down in it. Do not continue merely because nighttime has started; sleeping is the readiness check that the bed has been found and claimed.
steps.success_cue: The villager is visibly lying in the white bed, confirming that the high-altitude setup contains a villager with a claimed bed.

steps.action: Press T, enter the time command exactly as supplied, and press Enter, then wait for the villager to leave the bed.
steps.success_cue: It is daytime, the villager is awake and remains enclosed on the platform, and the bed remains intact.

steps.action: Double-tap Space to enable Creative flight, then stop providing movement input and verify that the player can hover without descending.
steps.success_cue: The player remains suspended when no movement key is held, confirming that Creative flight is active.

steps.action: Press T, enter the teleport command exactly as supplied, and press Enter. Remain hovering at that location; do not descend to the Superflat ground.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering around X=128.5, Y=200, Z=0.5, well away from the claimed bed, and no raid bar is visible.

steps.action: Press T, enter the effect command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to give the player Bad Omen for ten minutes.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that Bad Omen was applied and its status-effect indicator is present; no raid has started while the player remains at the remote location.

steps.action: Before returning, verify that the villager and bed have not been removed and that Creative flight is still active. Do not clear Bad Omen, change difficulty, or break any part of the glass village.
steps.success_cue: Bad Omen is active, the player is still hovering away from the village, and the sky-village setup remains intact.

steps.action: Press T, enter the teleport command exactly as supplied, and press Enter to enter the high-altitude village while Bad Omen is active. Stop issuing commands as soon as the Raid boss bar appears and hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering directly above the open-topped glass enclosure, the villager and claimed bed remain below, and the Raid boss bar has appeared.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just entered the Y=200 glass sky village while carrying Bad Omen, and the Raid boss bar has appeared. The villager and claimed bed are intact, Creative flight remains active, and no further commands or interactions have been performed; begin observing raid progression and entity activity now.
uncertainties: The report states only that the player-built village was high in the sky; it does not provide a seed, coordinates, exact height, village layout, or building materials. Y=200 in a default Superflat world and a glass enclosure were selected as a deterministic implementation of that condition.
The report does not specify game mode or difficulty. Creative mode was selected to construct and reach the test site safely, and Normal difficulty was selected to avoid Peaceful-mode ambiguity.

The exact Bad Omen acquisition method is not supplied. The version-compatible /effect command is used to reproduce the report's explicit statement that the reporter gave themselves Bad Omen without introducing patrol-spawn randomness.
A one-villager, one-claimed-bed setup is used as the minimum executable village. The written report does not state how many villagers, beds, job sites, or bells were in the reporter's original build.
The linked video and attachment contents were not supplied in the report text and were not used to infer additional geometry or timing requirements.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-266330:Loot Tables reset when reloading world | Relates:outward:MC-266287:Can't load .dat and .nbt files (server list & saved hotbar) | Duplicate:inward:MC-266325:Map data erased on restart | Duplicate:inward:MC-266332:Data files like raids, scoreboards, maps, etc. are not saved if they do not already exist | Duplicate:inward:MC-266375:Newly made maps won't save and throw exceptions to the log, when reloading into the save all affected maps are permanently blank. | Duplicate:inward:MC-266398:Maps cannot save
source_meta._title: Could not save data raids.dat and random_sequences.dat

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 23w44a in a single-player world using the integrated server. Use a newly created Overworld with commands enabled. Creative mode and Normal difficulty are practical choices for safe travel and reliable raid setup; the report does not specify a game mode or difficulty. Configure the launcher or test harness to retain the game's output log/stdout for the separate observation subsystem.
preconditions: Install or select the exact Java Edition snapshot 23w44a; do not use fix version 23w45a.
Use an unmodified client without mods or third-party server software.
Create a new world for this test rather than reusing a world that may already contain saved raid or random-sequence data.
Enable commands/cheats so the report's /locate and /effect commands can be executed.
Use a non-Peaceful difficulty; Normal is recommended as a practical inference.
Ensure the game process output or latest game log is retained for later inspection, but do not evaluate its contents during these reproduction steps.
Remain in the Overworld for the village and raid setup.
Do not defeat or intentionally cancel the raid before leaving the world.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using an installation configured for snapshot 23w44a. Wait for the main menu to finish loading and verify the displayed version before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is responsive and identifies the running version as 23w44a.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, assign the world a unique test name such as MC-266289-23w44a, select Creative mode, set difficulty to Normal, and enable commands/cheats. Do not add datapacks or reuse an existing world.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is configured for a new Creative, Normal-difficulty world with commands available.

steps.action: Create the world and wait without entering commands until terrain has rendered, the hotbar is visible, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a fully loaded new Overworld and can move normally.

steps.action: Press Esc once to pause the single-player game and open the Game Menu. Keep the captured game output available, but do not assess whether any particular error occurred.
steps.success_cue: The Game Menu is visible and the single-player game is paused.

steps.action: Choose Back to Game, or press Esc again, to close the pause menu.
steps.success_cue: The Game Menu has closed and normal player control has resumed.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the report's locate command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This must be run by the player in chat, not by a server console.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the nearest structure matching the village tag and displays bracketed coordinates containing an X and Z position.

steps.action: Record the X and Z coordinates returned by the locate command. Press T, enter the teleport command shown in exact_input after replacing <X> and <Z> with those returned integers, and press Enter. Keep Y set to 200 so the player arrives above terrain rather than inside an unknown block.
steps.success_cue: The player is teleported to X and Z matching the locate result, at approximately Y=200 above the destination area.

steps.action: Allow the player to descend safely in Creative mode, or double-tap Space to begin flying and hold Left Shift to descend under control. Wait for the destination chunks to render before searching the immediate area.
steps.success_cue: Terrain around the located coordinates is rendered, the player is in open air or safely on the terrain, and controls respond normally.

steps.action: Move into the located village. Identify it by the nearby group of village buildings and village features such as villagers, beds, workstations, paths, farms, or a bell. Stand among the village buildings rather than merely viewing them from a distance.
steps.success_cue: The player is physically within the village area among its buildings or villagers.

steps.action: Press T to open chat. Enter the Bad Omen command from the report exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Execute it only after entering the village so the default effect duration is not spent traveling.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that Bad Omen was applied to the player; the status-effect icon may appear briefly before the village consumes the effect to initiate the raid.

steps.action: Remain within the village and wait for raid initialization. Do not attack villagers, raid mobs, or otherwise attempt to finish the raid. Continue only after the raid boss bar has appeared at the top of the screen.
steps.success_cue: A raid boss bar is visible, confirming that a raid is active in the current village.

steps.action: While the raid boss bar is still visible, press Esc to open the Game Menu. Do not wait for the raid to finish.
steps.success_cue: The Game Menu is open while the world still contains the active raid established in the preceding step.

steps.action: Click Save and Quit to Title once. Wait until world shutdown completes and the main title screen is responsive; do not force-close the game process.
steps.success_cue: The world has closed normally and the main title screen is visible.

steps.action: From the title screen, click Singleplayer and wait for the world-selection list to appear.
steps.success_cue: The world-selection screen lists the test world created earlier.

steps.action: Select the same test world used to start the raid. Confirm its name matches the world created for this reproduction and do not create or select another world.
steps.success_cue: The original MC-266289 test world is highlighted in the world-selection list.

steps.action: Click Play Selected World, or double-click the highlighted test world, to reopen that same save.
steps.success_cue: The loading screen appears for the original test world.

steps.action: Wait until world loading and chunk rendering finish. Do not perform additional commands, change dimensions, apply another effect, or start another raid after loading. Stop execution as soon as the player can move and the village area is visible.
steps.success_cue: The same world has finished reloading, the player can move normally, and the surrounding village chunks are rendered.

stor.handoff_condition: The same 23w44a world has just been reopened after it was saved and exited while a raid boss bar was active. The village area is rendered, player controls are responsive, no post-load commands or interactions have occurred, and the captured game output remains available. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed or fixed village coordinates. The plan therefore uses the supplied /locate command and dynamically substitutes its returned X and Z coordinates into a practical teleport command.
The report does not specify game mode or difficulty. Creative mode and Normal difficulty are selected only to make travel safe and to avoid Peaceful difficulty interfering with raid setup.

The report says to find a village but does not specify how to travel to the locate result. Teleporting to Y=200 above the returned X/Z position is a practical inference and is not asserted as necessary for the bug.
A new world is selected to avoid pre-existing saved-data files affecting reproducibility; the report itself only says to open a world.

The report provides both an output-log reproduction and a raid-persistence reproduction. This plan includes the initial pause and log capture from the first route, then uses the more operationally explicit raid route for the final trigger and handoff.
The Windows filesystem path in the sample exception reflects the reporter's machine and is not treated as an operating-system requirement.
No external web verification was used because the exact affected version and version-specific /locate and /effect commands were supplied directly by the report.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-270020:Bad omen does not disappear when entering the village | Relates:outward:MC-270026:Raid omen of lower level is displayed in the GUI indefinitely after a raid has started with a higher omen level
source_meta._title: Bad Omen is not removed when experimental features are disabled

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w13a in a new single-player Superflat world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands enabled, Easy difficulty, raids enabled, and the "Update 1.21" experimental feature disabled.
preconditions: Use snapshot 24w13a exactly; do not use the listed fix version, 1.20.5 Pre-Release 1.
Create a new disposable test world rather than opening an important existing world.
Leave the "Update 1.21" experiment disabled. The experiment must not be enabled at any point for this reproduction.
Enable commands so the deterministic setup commands can be executed through in-game chat.
Use Easy difficulty rather than Peaceful so a raid can start while minimizing unnecessary raid waves.
The reproduction requires a village. This plan creates a minimal village using one villager and one bed claimed by that villager.
No world seed or coordinates are specified by the report.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, open the Installations page, enable the option that displays snapshot versions, and create or select an installation whose version is exactly snapshot 24w13a.
steps.success_cue: An installation explicitly labeled 24w13a is available in the launcher.

steps.action: Launch the 24w13a installation and wait for Minecraft to reach the title screen.
steps.success_cue: The title screen is responsive and identifies the running version as Minecraft 24w13a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then Create New World. Set Game Mode to Creative, enable commands or cheats, and set Difficulty to Easy. A suitable optional world name is "MC-269963".
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands: ON; Difficulty: Easy
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode, commands enabled, and Easy difficulty.

steps.action: Open the More tab, select Experiments, and inspect the "Update 1.21" toggle. Leave it OFF; if it is ON, click it once to turn it OFF. Select Done to return to world creation. Do not enable any experiment.
steps.success_cue: The world is configured without the Update 1.21 experimental data pack enabled.

steps.action: Open the World tab, set World Type to Superflat, and create the world. Wait until the terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a fully loaded, flat Overworld and can move normally.

steps.action: Ensure raids are enabled. Press T to open in-game chat, type the command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the disableRaids game rule is set to false.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to find a bed, place one bed such as a White Bed into an empty hotbar slot, and press E again to close the inventory. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: A bed is present in one of the nine hotbar slots and the inventory screen is closed.

steps.action: Select the bed's hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel. Aim at the top face of the flat ground and right-click once to place the bed. Make sure both halves of the bed appear and that open ground surrounds it.
steps.success_cue: A complete two-block-long bed is visible on the flat ground.

steps.action: Stand immediately beside the bed. Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter to summon a villager nearby.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that a villager was summoned, and one villager is visible within a few blocks of the bed.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter to make it nighttime so the villager can visibly claim and use the bed.
steps.success_cue: The world changes to nighttime while the villager and bed remain loaded.

steps.action: Move several blocks away from the bed without leaving the area, and wait until the villager reaches and lies in the bed. Keep the path to the bed unobstructed. If the villager cannot reach it, remove any obstruction and wait again; do not continue until the villager is sleeping.
steps.success_cue: The villager is visibly lying in the bed, confirming that the bed has been claimed and the minimal village exists.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Wait for the villager to leave the bed, but do not break the bed or remove the villager.
steps.success_cue: It is daytime, the villager is awake, and both the villager and its claimed bed remain present.

steps.action: Stand within two or three blocks of the claimed bed. Press T, enter the following relative teleport command including the leading slash, and press Enter. After teleporting, do not move horizontally; remaining at the destination is necessary so the inverse teleport returns to the same village position.
steps.success_cue: The player is now 160 blocks along the positive X direction from the claimed bed, the teleport command has completed, and the player has not moved horizontally afterward.

steps.action: While still at the distant position, press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter. This grants Bad Omen level I for 600 seconds without requiring a randomly generated raid captain.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that Bad Omen was applied to the player, and the Bad Omen status-effect icon is visible.

steps.action: Press E and verify that Bad Omen is listed among the player's active effects. Close the inventory with E. Do not drink milk, clear effects, die, change dimensions, or move horizontally before the next step.
steps.success_cue: Bad Omen is confirmed active, the inventory is closed, and the player remains at the teleport destination.

steps.action: Trigger the test by returning directly to the minimal village. Press T, enter the inverse relative teleport command including the leading slash, and press Enter. Make no further input after the teleport; hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as the player arrives and raid initiation begins.
steps.success_cue: The player has arrived back within a few blocks of the villager and its claimed bed after entering with Bad Omen active; raid initiation has been triggered and no effect-clearing action has been performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just returned to the claimed-bed village while Bad Omen level I was active, causing raid initiation under 24w13a with the Update 1.21 experiment disabled. Immediately hand off to the observation subsystem before using any command, consuming milk, dying, changing dimensions, leaving the village, or completing the raid.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce section, game mode, seed, coordinates, world type, or Bad Omen acquisition method. The plan reconstructs the minimum deterministic path supported by the description.

Creative mode, a Superflat world, Easy difficulty, an artificial one-villager village, and command-based effect application are practical execution choices rather than requirements explicitly stated by the report.

The plan grants Bad Omen directly with /effect instead of locating and killing a raid captain. This avoids random exploration while preserving the report's required pre-trigger state: the player has Bad Omen outside a village and then enters the village.

The report describes endlessly restarting raids as a consequence, but reproducing that consequence would require completing a full raid. The handoff occurs at the first raid initiation because that is the earliest point at which the reported Bad Omen removal failure can be inspected.

source_meta._title: If the raid begins more than 112 blocks above the ground, all illagers will be summoned and the player wins

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 in a fresh single-player Superflat world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode, enable commands/cheats, and select Normal difficulty. Do not use the fix snapshot 24w33a or a later version for the primary reproduction. Use default raid-related gamerules, with doMobSpawning enabled and disableRaids disabled.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher has an installation for the exact Java Edition 1.21 release.
No mods, datapacks, or server plugins are active.
A fresh Superflat world can be created so that the surface is level and the supplied relative teleport reliably puts the raid point more than 112 blocks above the ground.
Keyboard and mouse controls are available. If controls are rebound, use the bindings corresponding to Open Chat, Jump/Fly, Use Item, and Inventory.
Commands must be enabled because the report requires /tp and the deterministic setup uses additional commands.
Keep the world difficulty above Peaceful; Normal is selected for this plan.
Do not construct any additional solid platforms or spawnable blocks near the elevated enclosure.

steps.action: Launch the exact Minecraft Java Edition 1.21 release. From the title screen, select Singleplayer and create a new world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen for Java Edition 1.21 is open.

steps.action: Configure the new world as a fresh Superflat world. Set the game mode to Creative, allow commands/cheats, and set difficulty to Normal, then create the world. Leave the default Superflat preset unchanged.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Superflat; Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands/Cheats: On; Difficulty: Normal
steps.success_cue: The player loads into a new level Superflat world in Creative mode.

steps.action: Wait until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally. Stand directly on the grass surface, not on a structure or another placed block. Open the debug screen with F3 and record the player's displayed Y coordinate as the starting surface-level coordinate, then close the debug screen with F3.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding Superflat ground is fully visible, the player is standing on it, and the starting Y coordinate has been recorded.

steps.action: Enter Creative flight before teleporting so the player does not fall after arriving in midair. Double-tap the Jump control, which is Space by default, and rise slightly to confirm flight, then return to approximately the recorded standing height without landing elsewhere.
steps.success_cue: The player is hovering in Creative flight and does not fall when no movement key is held.

steps.action: While hovering above the original surface position, press T to open in-game chat, enter the report's teleport command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not move horizontally after teleporting because subsequent relative construction commands use this position as their center.
steps.success_cue: The player is teleported vertically upward and is hovering over the same ground location.

steps.action: Wait until the ground below and the surrounding chunk columns are rendered. Open the debug screen with F3 and verify that the displayed Y coordinate is 120 blocks higher than the coordinate recorded before the teleport, then close the debug screen. If the player is descending, immediately double-tap Space to resume Creative flight before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in the air 120 blocks above the original position, with the level ground visible far below.

steps.action: Create a small non-spawnable floor directly beneath the hovering player. Press T, enter the fill command exactly, and press Enter. The command creates a 7-by-7 glass floor one block below the current position.
steps.success_cue: A 7-by-7 glass platform appears immediately below the player and command feedback reports that blocks were filled.

steps.action: Stop flying by double-tapping the Jump control and settle onto the center of the new glass platform. Do not move horizontally away from the center until all four wall commands have been executed.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing at the center of the glass platform without falling.

steps.action: Construct the first two-block-high glass wall along one edge of the platform. Open chat, execute the command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A seven-block-wide, two-block-high glass wall exists along the platform edge at relative Z -3.

steps.action: Construct the opposite two-block-high glass wall. Open chat, execute the command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A matching glass wall exists along the opposite platform edge at relative Z +3.

steps.action: Construct the third two-block-high glass wall. Open chat, execute the command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A glass wall closes the platform edge at relative X -3.

steps.action: Construct the fourth two-block-high glass wall. Open chat, execute the command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is inside a roofless 5-by-5 interior surrounded by two-block-high glass walls, with no opening through which villagers can walk.

steps.action: Obtain two beds for the elevated village. Press T, execute the give command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Two Red Beds are present in the player's inventory and command feedback confirms that they were given.

steps.action: Obtain two villager spawn eggs. Press T, execute the give command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Two Villager Spawn Eggs are present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Obtain the item called an Ominous Bottle in Java Edition 1.21; this is the bottle that grants Bad Omen when consumed. Press T, execute the give command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: One Ominous Bottle is present in the player's inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Move the Red Beds, Villager Spawn Eggs, and Ominous Bottle into separate hotbar slots if they were not placed there automatically. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen. Close the inventory with E.
steps.success_cue: The beds, spawn eggs, and Ominous Bottle are visible in known hotbar slots and can be selected with the number keys or mouse wheel.

steps.action: Select the Red Bed in the hotbar. Inside the glass enclosure, right-click a glass floor block to place the first bed. Place the second bed parallel to the first on a separate pair of floor blocks. Each bed needs two unobstructed floor positions and open space above it; do not overlap the beds or place them against an arrangement that prevents villagers from reaching them.
steps.exact_input: Select Red Bed; right-click twice on two separate valid floor positions
steps.success_cue: Two complete Red Beds are visible inside the enclosure, with enough open floor space for villagers to approach them.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg. Right-click two separate exposed glass floor blocks inside the enclosure, once per egg, to create two villagers. Do not right-click an existing villager, because that can spawn a baby villager instead of the intended second adult.
steps.exact_input: Select Villager Spawn Egg; right-click an exposed floor block twice
steps.success_cue: Two adult villagers are alive inside the glass enclosure and cannot leave through the walls.

steps.action: Confirm deterministically that the villagers can claim and use the beds. Open chat, set the time to night, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The sky becomes dark and the world is at nighttime.

steps.action: Wait without moving the beds until both villagers navigate to and lie in the two beds. If a villager cannot reach a bed, remove and replace that bed within the enclosure with an unobstructed approach, then wait again. Do not continue until both villagers have demonstrated access to separate beds.
steps.success_cue: Both villagers are lying in separate beds, confirming that the elevated enclosure contains villagers with usable, claimed beds.

steps.action: Return the world to daytime while preserving the same villagers and beds. Press T, execute the time command, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Daylight returns, both villagers remain confined in the enclosure, and both beds remain in place.

steps.action: Select the Ominous Bottle in the active hotbar slot. The active slot is the hotbar slot outlined on the gameplay screen. Remain inside the elevated enclosure near the villagers and beds.
steps.exact_input: Select the hotbar slot containing minecraft:ominous_bottle
steps.success_cue: The Ominous Bottle is visible in the player's hand while the player stands inside the elevated village enclosure.

steps.action: Drink the Ominous Bottle by holding the Use Item control, which is right-click by default, until the drinking animation finishes and the bottle is consumed. Do not leave the enclosure and do not drink milk afterward.
steps.success_cue: The bottle has been consumed; Bad Omen is applied and, because the player is already within the bed-and-villager village, it changes into the timed Raid Omen effect.

steps.action: Remain inside the enclosure without breaking beds, moving villagers, descending toward the ground, or placing additional blocks. Wait through the Raid Omen countdown. Do not proceed based only on elapsed wall-clock time; wait until the Raid Omen effect expires and the raid interface begins.
steps.success_cue: Raid Omen has expired and a Raid boss bar has just appeared or begun its initial charge, while the player and both villagers remain in the elevated glass enclosure.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is still inside the glass enclosure approximately 120 blocks above the original Superflat surface; both villagers and both claimed beds remain present; the Raid Omen countdown has just expired; and the Raid boss bar has appeared or begun charging. Hand control to the observation subsystem now so it can monitor the first raid wave and subsequent raid progression without the reproduction agent moving, fighting, adding blocks, or descending to the ground.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a seed, world type, biome, game mode, difficulty, villager count, bed count, or exact enclosure design. This plan uses a fresh Superflat world, Creative mode, Normal difficulty, two adult villagers, two beds, and a 7-by-7 glass platform with a 5-by-5 enclosed interior as the simplest deterministic implementation of the reported setup.

The report's phrase 'bottle of bad omen' refers operationally to the Ominous Bottle item introduced for Java Edition 1.21. Drinking it grants Bad Omen, which changes to Raid Omen when the player is within a qualifying village.
Only the supplied /tp @s ~ ~120 ~ command comes directly from the report. The /fill, /give, and /time commands are practical setup choices and do not replace or alter the supplied teleport command.

The 120-block separation is relative to the player's starting position. This plan requires the player to begin directly on the level Superflat surface so the elevated village remains more than 112 blocks above the ground.

The report does not state whether Creative mode was used. Creative mode is selected to prevent an accidental fatal fall and to make construction deterministic; no Creative-only interaction is used after the raid countdown begins.
The report lists 24w33a as a fix version. It is intentionally excluded from recommended_version because the primary reproduction must be performed in the first listed affected version, 1.21.

source_meta._title: Raiders do not spawn on small islands even though there are close enough places around the village

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w33a in a new single-player world using the Default world type and seed 23925373020405760. Use Survival mode, Normal difficulty, and enable commands/cheats for deterministic setup. Do not use mods, datapacks, custom world generation, or a fix version such as 24w35a.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to start the historical Java Edition snapshot 24w33a.
Use a new world rather than an existing or upgraded world.
Use the exact positive seed 23925373020405760 and leave World Type set to Default.
Enable commands/cheats during world creation so the teleport, block placement, entity summon, and item-give commands can be executed.
Keep the default game tick rate and do not pause the game during timed Raid Omen or raid-start waiting periods.
The instructions assume the default Use Item control is right-click. If controls are rebound, use the key or mouse button assigned to Use Item instead.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the launcher installation configured for snapshot 24w33a. Do not select 24w35a, because that is listed as a fix version rather than an affected version.
steps.success_cue: The title screen identifies the running version as Minecraft Java Edition 24w33a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, open the world-generation settings, enter the report's seed, and make sure World Type is Default.
steps.success_cue: The create-world screen shows seed 23925373020405760 and the Default world type.

steps.action: Leave the game mode as Survival and the difficulty as Normal, enable Allow Commands or cheats, and create the world. Survival and Normal are controlled practical choices because the report does not specify game mode or difficulty; Normal is used to avoid Peaceful-mode interference while retaining ordinary raid gameplay.
steps.success_cue: The new world begins loading with commands available to the player.

steps.action: Wait without entering commands until the player has spawned, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally and the initial surrounding chunks are visible.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the teleport command including its leading slash, and press Enter. This implements the report's instruction to teleport to X=204, Y=65, Z=110.
steps.success_cue: The player is teleported to the island area at 204 65 110 and the command reports successful teleportation.

steps.action: Do not modify the terrain. Wait until the terrain around the destination has rendered and player movement and commands respond normally. The player may settle slightly below Y=65 if gravity moves them after teleportation.
steps.success_cue: The small-island terrain around coordinates 204 65 110 is fully visible and responsive.

steps.action: Open chat with T and place the required composter at the report's exact block coordinates by running the command below. Include the leading slash and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A composter occupies block X=202, Y=62, Z=111, and chat reports that the block was placed or changed.

steps.action: Open chat and summon one ordinary villager centered on the horizontally adjacent block immediately east of the composter. The report only says to summon the villager beside the composter; X=203.5, Y=62, Z=111.5 is the deterministic adjacent position selected for this plan.
steps.success_cue: One living adult villager is visible beside the composter and chat reports that a villager was summoned.

steps.action: Remain nearby and allow the villager to detect and claim the composter. Look for the brief green linking particles and/or the villager changing from unemployed clothing to the farmer profession. Do not remove the composter or allow the villager to die. A villager linked to a job-site block is sufficient to establish the raid-relevant village condition. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AAdvancement_guide/Adventure_tab?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The villager is alive near the composter and visibly has the farmer profession, confirming that the composter has been claimed.

steps.action: Open chat and give the player two ordinary Ominous Bottles so one is available for the first attempt and one is reserved for the report's requested repeat. Include the leading slash and press Enter. The Java Edition item identifier is ominous_bottle, and an unmodified bottle uses the default lowest amplifier. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/%E7%89%A9%E5%93%81%E5%A0%86%E5%8F%A0%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E6%A0%BC%E5%BC%8F?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that two Ominous Bottles were given, and the inventory contains a stack of two bottles.

steps.action: Return the player to the report's test position without moving the villager or composter. Open chat, execute the exact command, and wait for movement to stabilize.
steps.success_cue: The player is back at or settling immediately around 204 65 110, within the test village area, while the villager remains alive and linked to the composter.

steps.action: Close chat. Locate the stack of two Ominous Bottles in the nine-slot hotbar at the bottom of the screen. Select its slot using the corresponding number key 1 through 9 or the mouse wheel so the bottle is held in the player's hand.
steps.success_cue: An Ominous Bottle is visible in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted; the stack count is 2 before drinking.

steps.action: While remaining near the villager and composter, hold Use Item—right-click by default—until the drinking animation completes and one bottle is consumed. Do not walk away during or after consumption. Drinking an Ominous Bottle grants Bad Omen, which converts to the approximately 30-second Raid Omen countdown when the player is in a recognized village. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/ominous-bottle?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The bottle-consumption sound and animation finish, the held stack decreases from 2 to 1, and the player receives Raid Omen with a countdown near 30 seconds.

steps.action: Keep the player near coordinates 204 65 110 and leave the villager, composter, terrain, and remaining bottle untouched. Do not pause the game. Wait until the Raid Omen countdown completes and the Raid boss bar appears. This transition starts the raid and its spawn-location search. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/ominous-bottle?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The Raid boss bar has just appeared while the player remains beside the prepared small-island village; begin observation immediately without evaluating the raider outcome in this setup plan.

stor.handoff_condition: The first Raid boss bar has just appeared at the small-island village, the farmer villager is alive and linked to the composter at 202 62 111, the player remains near 204 65 110, and one unused Ominous Bottle remains in inventory. The observation subsystem should now monitor the unchanged setup for at least 60 seconds. To preserve the report's requested repeat, once the first raid lifecycle and its UI are no longer active, the observation subsystem should select the reserved bottle, consume it while remaining beside the same villager and composter, wait through the next Raid Omen countdown, and observe the second raid-start window without rebuilding or moving the village.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode or difficulty. This plan uses Survival mode and Normal difficulty with commands enabled as a practical deterministic configuration.
The report does not provide the exact position at which the villager was summoned, only that it was beside the composter. This plan uses the center of the adjacent block at 203.5 62 111.5.

The report does not state an Ominous Bottle level. This plan uses the ordinary default Ominous Bottle, corresponding to the lowest default amplifier, and reserves a second identical bottle for the requested repeat.

The report asks to wait approximately one minute and then repeat the bottle-and-wait sequence. Because observation must begin as soon as the raid starts, that timed waiting period and the repeated attempt are delegated to the observation subsystem in the handoff condition.

The villager must claim the composter before the bottle is consumed. If the villager never becomes a farmer, the raid village precondition has not been reached and the trigger steps must not be executed.
